rule: Nothing fetched here is committed as bytes. The manifest is the warrant: re-fetch, compare the SHA-256, and the reading is reproducible without this repository republishing anyone's document or anyone's bug report.
raw_cache: outside the repository (--raw), never inside it

sources.name: triage-bugzilla.html
sources.what: Mozilla's Bugzilla triage policy: who triages, within what timeframe, and the institution's own definition of a triaged bug. This is the norm tonight measures against, and it is the reason tonight may use the word 'late' at all — it names one week, so no threshold has to be taken out of the distribution.

sources.name: bug-types.html
sources.what: The definitions of the three bug types and the sentence that names a different applier for each branch: 'Engineering triages defects and tasks. Product management triages enhancements.'

sources.name: severity.html
sources.what: The severity scale in force, for the vocabulary P5(a) tests the window against.

sources.name: priority.html
sources.what: The priority scale, read alongside severity so that the un-normed state is not confused with an un-prioritised one.

sources.name: field-bug_severity.json
sources.what: The machine-readable list of legal severity values. It still contains the pre-2020 vocabulary (blocker, critical, major, normal, minor, trivial, enhancement) alongside S1-S4, which is why P5(a) is a real check and not a formality: the old values remain assignable.

sources.name: field-bug_type.json
sources.what: The machine-readable list of legal type values: '--', defect, enhancement, task. The '--' is the reporter declining to choose a branch at all.

sources.name: bug-1522348.json
sources.what: 'Bulk assign open bugs to task, enhancement, defect field' — the migration that gave a type to bugs filed before the field existed. Fetched to date it, so the window can be shown to start after it rather than merely asserted to.

sources.name: population.json
sources.what: The population W: every publicly visible bug created in [2024-01-01, 2025-07-01) in the seven products named in PREDICTIONS.md, 67272 rows over 72 paginated requests. Cached outside the repository; only aggregates and one named falsifier population are committed.
sources.note: 72 requests, 31438784 bytes over the wire, 0 duplicate rows dropped

sources.name: history.json
sources.what: The full change history of 300 of 300 sampled bugs (seed 20260829, drawn from the harvested id list). This is the only way to ask whether the value in a field is the one the person filing put there.
sources.note: 0 ids returned no history and are listed in the cache

sources.name: creators.json
sources.what: Who filed each bug in W and who it is assigned to, fetched in a second pass after the first results showed a confound the predictions had not anticipated. Used only to ask whether the filer and the assignee are the same person.
